title: introduce-session-affinity-and-compact-cred-adapter-for-cross-sdk-streams
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds session-affinity header to SDK streaming handshakes; introduces a compact credential adapter used by Python/TS/Go SDKs to reduce auth handshake size and improve reauth latency. Minor SDK version bumps: py 1.9.4 -> 1.10.0, ts 2.4.7 -> 2.5.0, go v0.8.3 -> v0.9.0.
description: Context: Several customers hit intermittent stream reconnects under high multiplexed workloads when token rotation and per-request routing caused the server to open new session allocations. This PR implements a lightweight session-affinity hint in the streaming handshake plus a compact credential adapter that centralizes token rotation logic across Python/TS/Go SDKs to reduce on-wire auth chatter and make reauth deterministic. The change is intentionally backward-compatible: servers ignore unknown affinity headers, and the adapter exposes a pluggable interface for custom KMS/HSM hooks. What this PR does: - Add session-affinity header (X-Redwood-Session-Affinity) to initial stream bootstrap and persist it in reconnect attempts - Introduce compact credential adapter (CompactCredProvider) shared design across SDKs; language-specific implementations included - Normalize retry/backoff profiles used by streaming reconnects to avoid synchronized thundering restarts; add jitter and an exponential floor for short-lived tokens - Bump SDK versions (py/ts/go) and update changelogs - Add integration tests (e2e streaming with simulated short-lived tokens) and new unit tests for adapter and affinity fallback Migration notes: servers will ignore affinity if not supported; customers with custom proxies should ensure affinity headers are preserved through routing. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: linear/ENG-9283 linked - [x] Language implementations: python/typescript/go - [x] Unit tests added and passing - [x] Integration tests: streaming-e2e added - [x] Metrics: added affinity.sent, affinity.fallback, cred.rotate.duration - [x] Changelog entries and SDK version bumps - [x] Security review: token handling audit done (SUP-4572) Links: design/notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9283/session-affinity-design e2e run: https://ci.internal.redwood/job/streaming-e2e/401821
commits: 3 commits: 1) session: add affinity header and handshake persistence (m.chen) 2) auth: introduce compact cred adapter interface + go/python/ts impls (m.chen) 3) tests: add streaming-e2e and flakiness mitigations (r.patel)
discussion: Rhea: Can we guarantee the header survives common proxies (Envoy/LB)? Reply (Maya): We added an integration test that runs through a simulated Envoy path and also documented the requirement in docs/sdk/migration/session-affinity.md. If customers use strict header stripping they must whitelist the header. Noah: The backoff normalization looks good, but what about tokens that rotate faster than our floor? Reply (Maya): Added an exponential floor and a fast-rotate hint in the adapter; fast-rotate callers can opt-in to tighter restart windows via the provider interface. Diego: Minor nit: tighten type on the TS adapter to avoid any on public surface. Action: updated types and added tests. Rhea: CI flaky on first run (intermittent e2e timeout). Status: retried job, all checks green and integration flake fixed by increasing test harness timeouts and adding retry for transient network error. Approvals: +1 Noah, +1 Diego, +1 Rhea. Merge: squash and merge after CI green.
notes_on_testing: Local unit test matrix: python 3.10/3.11, node 18, go 1.20. Integration e2e runs against internal harness with short-lived token simulator; observed ~35% fewer reconnects in synthetic load compared to baseline. Metrics added: affinity.sent, affinity.fallback, cred.rotate.duration. Telemetry: added debug logs behind feature flag for first 48h post-release.
upgrade_instructions: Python: pip install redwood==1.10.0 and ensure proxies forward X-Redwood-Session-Affinity header. Typescript: npm i @redwood/sdk@2.5.0 and rebuild consumers. Go: go get github.com/redwood/sdk@v0.9.0. If you run private deployments, upgrade server to >= release-2026-02 to honor affinity header; otherwise servers will ignore the header with no functional regressions.
security_review: token handling and adapter surface underwent a quick security audit by security team (SUP-4572). Minor finding: ensure adapter implementations don't log tokens; fixed and added test to prevent token leakage in logs.
backports: cherry-pick candidate for release/2026-02; backport patch available in branches/release/1.10.x for python and release/2.5.x for typescript.
